previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was readmitted with fevers, hypotension, and respiratory distress following recent discharge for MSSA sepsis. He was found to have Pseudomonas pneumonia and persistent pleural effusion, requiring ICU monitoring, antibiotics, and temporary CVVH due to hypotension during dialysis. A thoracentesis was performed, showing inflammatory fluid. Sputum cultures confirmed Pseudomonas, and treatment was continued with piperacillin-tazobactam, vancomycin, and ciprofloxacin. His anemia was managed with a blood transfusion. He stabilized after 24 hours, resumed regular hemodialysis, and was discharged to an extended care facility on IV antibiotics, with plans for ongoing dialysis, seizure medication adherence, and close monitoring for clinical deterioration.

radiology_notes.text:

terminating within the right atrium, slightly more cranial in position than on
the prior study.  A left-sided PIC catheter has been removed.  There is

There is slight cephalization of the pulmonary vasculature.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Right lower lobe opacity, similar to the prior examinations; however, new

follow-up to resolution after appropriate treatment.  Small right pleural

2.  Slightly more cranial position of a femoral catheter with its tip in the

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  ___ male with history of end-stage renal
disease on hemodialysis with right tunneled common femoral dialysis catheter.
Patient presents with high-grade bacteremia.  Request for line removal.

OPERATORS:  The procedure was performed by Dr. ___.  Dr. ___,
___ attending radiologist, reviewed the study.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  A timeout was performed with two patient identifiers.
The patient was placed supine on the gurney and the right groin and indwelling
dialysis catheter were prepped and draped in usual sterile fashion.
Approximately 15 cc of lidocaine was administered to the tunneled site.  Blunt
dissection was performed around the catheter and the catheter cuffs.  Gentle
pressure was used to remove the catheter and pressure was placed at the right
common femoral venous entry site for approximately 15 minutes.  A sterile
dressing was applied over the puncture site.  There were no post-procedural
complications.

IMPRESSION:
Successful removal of a tunneled right common femoral hemodialysis catheter.
The tip was sent for culture.

HISTORY:  Right groin ultrasound

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis from ___.

FINDINGS:  Color and Doppler sonograms were performed in the region of the
right groin.  There is normal appearance to the common femoral artery, common
femoral vein, and greater saphenous vein.  No evidence for fistula formation. 
In the superficial tissues of the right groin is a predominantly hypoechoic
tubular structure with linear echogenic wall, and no measurable vascular flow,
compatible with a clotted old AV graft, which was present on the prior CT
examination.  There is an enlarged 2.7 x 0.9 cm node within the right groin. 
However, there are no fluid collections.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No pseudoaneurysm, or fluid collections.  There is an enlarged lymph node
within the right groin.
2.  Clotted AV graft within the right leg, present on prior CT examination.

HISTORY:  Patient is a ___ male with history of end-stage renal
disease on hemodialysis, recently admitted with line sepsis.  His right
femoral tunneled dialysis catheter was removed on ___.  The patient now
requires new access for hemodialysis.

Of note, decision was made in conjunction with the clinical team to place a
non-tunneled, temporary hemodialysis catheter.  This was done as the patient's
potassium level was 5.9, and it was felt safer to postpone sedation for line
tunneling until after hemodialysis and correction of electrolyte disturbance.

OPERATORS:  Dr. ___ (resident) and Dr. ___.  Dr.
___ radiologist, was present and monitoring the entire procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  1% local lidocaine and 50 mcg of fentanyl.  The patient's
hemodynamic parameters were monitored continuously throughout the course of
the procedure.

FINDINGS:

After the risks and benefits of the procedure were explained in detail to the
patient, written informed consent was obtained.  The patient was then brought
to the angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging table.  The
patient's left groin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A
preprocedure timeout and huddle were performed as per standard ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance with hard copy images on file, the left femoral vein
was accessed with a micropuncture needle.  Microwire was passed into the
inferior vena cava, and the needle was exchanged for a micropuncture sheath.
The microwire and inner dilator were then removed from the sheath, and a short
___ wire was advanced into the inferior vena cava.  Microsheath was then
removed, and the tract was progressively dilated to 14 ___.  A 24 cm
hemodialysis catheter was then inserted over the wire and advanced into the
lower IVC.  The wire was removed. Ports were aspirated and flushed easily. The
line was secured to the skin with ___ silk sutures.  A sterile dressing was
applied.  

The patient tolerated the procedure well, there were no immediate post-
procedure complications.

IMPRESSION:  

Successful placement of non-tunneled left femoral hemodialysis catheter with
fluoro and ultrasound guidance. Total length is 24 cm tip to cuff.  The line
is ready for use, with the tip in the lower IVC.

After resolution of electrolyte disturbance, the patient should return to
interventional radiology for conversion to a tunneled line.

MEDICAL HISTORY:  ___ male with end-stage renal disease and left groin
temporary HD catheter in place.  A request was placed for conversion of left
femoral temporal line to a tunneled HD catheter before plan of discharge.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___.  Dr. ___ is the
attending radiologist who was present and supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
25 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of versed throughout the total intraservice time
of 20 minutes during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored.  Local anesthesia with 1% lidocaine and 1% lidocaine
with epinephrine.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  An informed written consent was obtained after
explaining the procedure, benefits, alternatives and risks involved.  The
patient was brought to angiography suite and placed supine on the imaging
table.  The left groin including the existing temporary HD catheter were
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure huddle and
timeout were performed as per ___ protocol.

An initial scout image was obtained demonstrating the existing temporary HD
catheter terminating in the distal IVC.  Both ports were aspirated to remove
the heparin and flushed with saline.  After instilling local anesthesia a
subcutaneous tunnel was created from the ___ aspect of left upper
thigh to the venous access site.  A double-lumen HD catheter measuring 50 cm
in length from tip to cuff was tunneled through and brought out at venous
access site.  Then a super stiff Amplatz guidewire was placed through one of
the ports of the temporary HD catheter and advanced into proximal IVC and
catheter removed over the guidewire.  A peel away sheath was placed over the
guidewire.  The inner dilator and the guidewire were removed and the catheter
placed through the peel-away sheath and advanced into right atrium.  The peel-
away sheath was then removed.  Both ports of the catheter were easily
aspirated and flushed.  The catheter was secured to skin with 0 silk sutures
and the wound over the venous access site in the left groin sutured with ___
Vicryl.  Sterile dressings were applied.  Fluoroscopic spot images were
obtained demonstrating satisfactory placement and position of the catheter and
stored digitally.  The patient tolerated the procedure well with no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Successful conversion of left common femoral venous temporary
line to a tunneled HD catheter via the left common femoral venous access.  The
tip to cuff length of the catheter is 50 cm and tip is terminating in the
right atrium.  The line is ready for use.
